topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and introduces the lecture topic while addressing the subject's complexity and context within the course.

topics.label: Complement fundamentals and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the general purpose, nomenclature rules, and central biochemical importance of C3 in the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms of the three recognition routes that trigger the complement cascade.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the functional mechanisms through which activated complement eliminates pathogens and promotes an immune response.

topics.label: Regulation of complement activation on host cells
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the molecular mechanisms that regulate complement activation to protect host tissues from self-damage.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how deficiencies in individual complement components lead to distinct clinical presentations and infection risks.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens evolve mechanisms to circumvent complement-mediated immune destruction, exemplified by Staphylococcus aureus.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
